title: Largest schematic open subspace of an algebraic space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Open subspaces of $X$ and their inclusion order are [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. There exists a largest open subspace $X^{\mathrm{sch}}\subseteq X$ represented by a scheme: $X^{\mathrm{sch}}$ is an open subspace whose sheaf is represented by a scheme, and every open subspace of $X$ whose sheaf is represented by a scheme is contained in $X^{\mathrm{sch}}$. No quasi-separatedness, finite-type or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed; $X^{\mathrm{sch}}$ may be empty.

source.place: Tag 03JH (lemma-subscheme), over the base Spec k.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open] to the algebraic space $X$ over $S$: it gives an open subspace $X_{\mathrm{sch}}\subseteq X$ represented by an $S$-scheme and containing every open subspace of $X$ represented by an $S$-scheme, with no separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis, possibly empty. Open subspaces are sheaves on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$, so a scheme representing one is an object of $\mathit{Sch}/S$, i.e. an $S$-scheme; thus the two notions of "represented by a scheme" agree and $X^{\mathrm{sch}}=X_{\mathrm{sch}}$ is the required largest schematic open subspace.
